gaps.wanted: The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only.

A photograph of the AC-powered 48YM and its JPSU-850W-AC supply. The studio photograph is of a DC unit; the AC supply is drawn from the guide's figures and the 650 W supply's photograph, and its size is the bay's.
What the yellow label, its hazard triangle and the light-blue bar at the right of the port side say. The guide's text names none; the label's text does not resolve at 3.2 px/mm.

The USB revision. The guide names one USB port and gives no generation. The port is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin because the tongue colour follows the photograph (qfx5120-48ym-rear-high.jpg), which shows a black tongue, not the blue of a USB 3.0 port.
The vertical rating label at the right edge of the rear (an AC input line, a DC input line and a line about each power supply). It is only partly legible in the photograph and is not drawn.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, sfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: guide Table 9: 1.72 in (4.37 cm) high, 17.36 in (44.09 cm) wide, 20.48 in (52.02 cm) deep excluding the fan and power supply handles, 24.8 lb (11.25 kg) with two supplies and the fans. The width is the body: the table says the outer edges of the front mounting brackets extend it to 19 in, so the brackets are not part of the body and are not modelled.

colour.note: The same face colour as the 48Y, #8b8f96, whose photograph is sharper; this photograph's plate is a similar cool grey. The rear panel's #7a7c82 is the 48Y's.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide lists the rack mount kit JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E (shipped with the switch; also sold as EX-4PST-RMK) and flush, recessed and two-post mounting; the library holds no kit contract for it and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out. The modelled body is the 440.9 mm chassis, without brackets.

front-labels.note: A yellow rectangular label at the right (407.8 to 430.5 mm, 2.8 to 8.1 mm down) and the laser hazard triangle beside it, and a light-blue bar at the right edge (437.0 to 438.8 mm, 12.1 to 34.9 mm down). The label's text is not legible at this resolution and is not drawn. The guide's text names none of the three; the 48Y front photograph shows none, so they are this panel's.

gate-1.note: The front photograph measures 1416 x 140 px between the body edges, an aspect of 10.1 against the table's 440.9 / 43.7 = 10.09; scale 3.21 px/mm across. The rear measures 1427 px wide, 3.237 px/mm. The photographs are low resolution, so the vertical positions are the weaker axis, anchored on the cage block: its 25.0 mm height between the first row's top and the second row's bottom agrees with the 48Y's 24.4 on the sharper photograph.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement for the QFX5120-48YM. No Juniper notice was found and the guide states none; the third-party trackers consulted list dates only for the QFX5120-48Y. Estimated, because an absence of notices on the pages searched is not the maker's statement.

mgmt-labels.note: The upper management jack is printed C1 above it and the lower C0 below it on this device, the reverse of the 48Y. The guide's callouts name them without saying which is on top.

modules.note: The 48YM takes 850 W supplies (JPSU-850W-AC-AFO and -AFI for AC), NOT the 650 W supplies of the 48T and 48Y (guide Table 25 and Table 7). The fan modules (QFX5110-FANAFO and -FANAFI) are the same as the 48Y's. All are bays; nothing on the chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay.

port-lamps.note: One lamp per port, in that strip, before its arrow (Tables 20 and 21: one lamp for each SFP28 port and each QSFP28 port, green steady with a link and blinking with activity, yellow blinking for the beacon). The 48Y has two to four per port; the 48YM has one. The entries sit at half the cage pitch for SFP28 (7.12 mm), the upper cage's lamp 3.5 mm into the cage's cell and the lower cage's 3.5 mm into its half; the QSFP28 entries are 8.9 mm apart within a column (the first lamp 5.0 mm into the cell) and 10.0 between columns, with the gutter between the pairs. A lamp is followed 2.1 mm on by its arrow (1.25 mm wide) and 4.2 mm on by its numeral. Positions are read off the photograph at 3.2 px/mm and are estimated to 0.3 mm.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal, read off the photograph and matching guide figure 37: the SFP28 ports run 0 to 23 down each column of the left block (even in the upper cage, odd in the lower), then the QSFP28 ports 48 to 55 in the middle block (48 and 49 in the first column, and so on), then the SFP28 ports 24 to 47 in the right block. All numerals are printed in ONE strip beneath the lower row, each with a lamp before it and an up or down arrow naming the cage it belongs to - an up arrow for the upper cage, a down arrow for the lower - two entries to a column. Interface names are not printed and the guide held does not state them; none is written here.

ports.note: Front photograph: three blocks. 24 SFP28 in twelve columns on the registry's 14.25 mm pitch from x 6.9 to 177.9; then the eight QSFP28 in four columns on the registry's 19.0 pitch in two pairs, the first pair starting at 180.5 and the second at 221.6 (a 3.1 mm gutter between the pairs); then 24 more SFP28 from 262.5 to 433.5. The block starts are fitted to the lamp strip beneath, whose 48 dark lamps fall on a pitch of 7.12 mm (7.11 over the first block and 7.14 over the last) with the first at 10.44 and the right block's first at 266.04, and to the cage openings' edges. The 48Y, a different front panel with the same cages, reads its SFP28 pitch to 0.01 mm of the registry's on its sharper photograph.

power.note: Table 30 (AC supplies, QFX5120-48YM): 280 W typical, 291 W with MACsec, and 446 W maximum, 460 W with MACsec; the maximum is measured at 40 C with SR optics and 100 percent IMIX load, the typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load, excluding transceivers. Input 100 to 240 VAC at 7.5 A (100 V) or 3 A (240 V). Table 40 (DC supplies): 333 W typical and 356 W maximum, 16 A, rated -48 to 60 VDC. The device states the non-MACsec pair of the AC table, the default build's, and keeps the rest as text. The two tables carry different figures for one box and neither names its scope beyond the note above, so both are kept.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 3.237 px/mm, checked against guide figure 36 and the callouts of figure 38. A 63.5 mm panel at the left carries the four chassis lamps, the RJ-45 console jack with the USB port beneath it in one shield, the two stacked RJ-45 management jacks, the ESD point, the PPS OUT and 10M OUT jacks and the reset pinhole; then five fan slots numbered 0 to 4 on a 49.0 mm pitch and the two supply slots, as on the 48Y. The orange fan faces measure 41.4 to 41.7 mm wide here against 40.8 to 41.0 on the 48Y's sharper photograph; the 48Y's are used for both, since the module is one part.

rear-photo-vs-drawing.note: The studio rear photograph is a DC-powered, front-to-back unit (terminal-block supplies, AIR OUT, Juniper Gold handles). The default configuration is the AC front-to-back build, whose supply is drawn from the guide's figure 71 and 75 because no photograph of an AC 48YM was found: see the supply's own contract. The DC supplies are not modelled.

row-pitch.note: SFP28 rows are 14.0 mm apart, the figure read on the 48Y's sharper photograph; this photograph's cage block, 9.3 to 34.3 mm, agrees. The QSFP28 pairs show a mesh divider between their rows (the photograph), so they are placed 15.0 mm apart, the registry's belly-to-belly figure, which closes the block on the same 34.3 mm bottom edge. The y origin is the top edge of the face at 36 px, good to about 0.3 mm.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5120 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-09-30, 339 pages (copyright HPE): the front and rear figures 35 to 40, Table 7 (models and variants), Table 9 (physical specifications), the LED sections (Tables 11, 13, 20, 21, 24, 34), the airflow tables 23 and 26 and the power tables 30 and 40, and the section on connecting 1-PPS and 10-MHz measurement devices. Juniper's studio photographs of the 48YM, front and rear, 1500 x 216 and 1500 x 228 px (image library, qfx5120-48ym-front-high and -rear-high): LOW RESOLUTION, 3.2 px/mm, so every position read off them is good to about 0.3 mm. THE HPE DATASHEET (a00150810enw) DID NOT ANSWER, a transport error on the one attempt, so no datasheet figure is used. No mechanical drawing and no 3D model were found. No end-of-sale announcement for the QFX5120-48YM was found on the manufacturer's pages, and the guide states none.

stack-orientation.note: The light latch tongues sit at the foot of each upper cage and at the top of each lower, so both lips face the band between the rows: upper cage upright, lower turned 180, the library's stack convention, read off the device. The QSFP28 pairs show the same, with the mesh divider between.

timing-jacks.note: Guide, Connecting 1-PPS and 10-MHz Measurement Devices to the QFX5120 Switch: the 48T and 48YM carry one 2x1 DIN 1.0/2.3 connector set with a PPS OUT and a 10M OUT port, TTL (5 V) and a cable up to 3 m. Two 1.0/2.3 jacks are placed, PPS OUT above 10M OUT. The photograph shows gold connectors with a round nut about 7 mm across, which agrees with that jack's nut.

vents.note: A row of round holes along the top edge (2.2 to 5.0 mm down, about 3.2 mm on pitch) and a row cut by the bottom edge (40.6 to 43.4 mm). Drawn as two vent strips.
